full_judgment:
Mr. M. M. Ruhul Amin, J.: These appeals by leave are directed against the judgment and decree dated 17.11.1994 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal Nos.226, 225, 228, 227, 222 & 221 of 1993 dismissing the same. The First Appeal were filed against the judgment and decree dated 31.07.1993 in Artha Rin Suit Nos.158, 156, 161, 160, 155 & 159 of 1991 of the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj. 

 4. The trial court on consideration of the evidence on record dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 31.07.1993. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff-appellant filed the above mentioned appeals and after hearing the High Court Division by the impugned judgments dated 17.11.1994 dismissed the appeals and affirmed the judgment passed by the trial Court. 

 5. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the plaintiff-appellant having prove the claim in the suits by adducing both oral and documentary evidence and the defendant-respondent No.2 having not denied the claim of the plaintiff in the aforesaid suit by deposing in the Court the High Court Division erred in law in affirming the judgments of the trial Court passed relying on the averments made in the written statement and on mere surmises and conjectures without properly considering the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the plaintiff-appellant and in brushing aside the admission of the defendant made in the written statements holding that the admission cannot be conclusive and must be held to be false by drawing inference that the defendant did not apply for letter of credit for importing the goods which was contrary to evidence and the further submission that in the absence of any evidence to show that fraud was practiced on the Respondents in obtaining blank signed forms as claimed by respondents; both the Courts acted illegally in dismissing the suits and the further submissions that both the Courts below failed to appreciate that in any event blank signed forms have the effect of granting power to fill in the same as in the case of blank Cheque and blank forms followed by filled informs have the effect of making defendant-respondents liable in law to pay the dues of the plaintiff claimed in the suit and as such the suits ought to have been decreed and the further submission that both the Courts below misconstrued the plaintiff's exhibited documents in the suit and thus failed to exercise proper jurisdiction specially when defendant-respondents did not give any oral evidence or documents to controvert the same and as such was not justified in dismissing the suits.
